result.title: Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL
result.summary: Text-to-SQL systems typically assume a one-to-one mapping between natural-language queries and correct SQL translations. In practice, however, many queries are inherently ambiguous, admitting multiple valid interpretations that yield distinct outputs. We introduce Adversarial Intent Resolution (AIR), a multi-agent framework that actively probes and resolves such ambiguity without any task-specific training. AIR first constructs competing interpretations, verifies through SQL execution that they produce genuinely different results, and generates targeted clarification questions grounded in the observed data differences. Evaluating on leading benchmarks for ambiguous questions, AIR demonstrates strong performance, efficiency, and robust cross-benchmark transferability. On the AMBROSIA benchmark under schema-only context, a realistic production setting where exposing the full database is infeasible, AIR outperforms IntentRL, the state-of-the-art reinforcement learning model, across all metrics (e.g., F1 0.679 vs. 0.618). Crucially, AIR exhibits only ~7% performance degradation without the full database, compared to ~20% for IntentRL. On the AmbiQT benchmark, where ambiguity arises from schema design rather than linguistic structure, AIR achieves higher F1 under both context settings without any benchmark-specific adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 Text-to-SQL 中自然语言查询的固有歧义，提出免任务训练的多智能体框架 AIR：先构造多个竞争解释，用 SQL 执行验证其结果确实不同，再据数据差异生成有针对性的澄清问题，在 AMBROSIA、AmbiQT 等歧义基准上优于 IntentRL 等模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「构造多个竞争解释—执行验证—生成澄清问题」的流程，可能与 LVR 中多 latent 假设的筛选、视觉证据获取与是否停止/追问的决策存在概念对应，可供核查能否迁移到视觉证据场景。
